breakdown_notes: The paper is Autor, Dorn & Hanson (2013), 'The China Syndrome: Local Labor Market Effects of Import Competition in the United States' (AER). It is a cross-sectional econometrics paper analyzing US commuting zones; the unit of analysis is 722 commuting zones x 2 time periods (N=1,444, stated explicitly in the paper: 'N = 1,444 (722 CZs x 2 time periods)'). The paper reports NO computational hardware, wall-clock time, GPU/CPU details, API usage, or runtime figures anywhere in the text, experiments, or appendix -- consistent with a 2013 applied-economics paper whose original analysis is Stata .do files reading .dta files. The replication plan reimplements the shipped Stata regressions in Python (pandas + linearmodels weighted 2SLS with state-clustered SEs). All inputs are pre-built .dta files totaling ~2.1MB on disk (largest is workfile_china.dta at 1.3MB). Every step is a small weighted 2SLS or OLS regression / summary statistic over at most ~1,444 rows -- these execute in milliseconds to a few seconds each. The plan states explicitly: 'No GPU is needed -- this is small-N commuting-zone econometrics (722 CZs x 2 periods); the RTX A6000s are irrelevant.' There are no training or ML-inference steps, no repeated runs over seeds/configs, and no external LLM API calls. Total end-to-end runtime is dominated by the one-time pip install of dependencies (pandas, numpy, scipy, linearmodels, statsmodels, openpyxl); the actual regression compute is well under 5 minutes on a single CPU core. No cost lookup is warranted (no GPU, no paid API).
dataset_size: ~2.1 MB total of pre-built Stata .dta files (workfile_china.dta 1.3MB, sic87dd_trade_data.dta 1.4MB, others smaller); analysis sample N=1,444 (722 commuting zones x 2 periods)
estimated_wall_clock: Under 5 minutes on a single CPU core (regressions run in seconds; runtime is dominated by one-time dependency install). No GPU, no network/API calls.
resource_type: CPU-only econometrics (small-N weighted 2SLS with cluster-robust SEs)
